data.name: Dex
data.detailed_description:
Explore, fight, talk and hack your way through a rich cyberpunk world in this 2D action-RPG!

Wanted dead by a mysterious and far-reaching organization, you will traverse the futuristic city of Harbor Prime and make unexpected allies on your quest to bring down the system! In this cyberpunk adventure inspired by Blade Runner and Neuromancer, you are free to choose your playstyle: will you be a silent assassin, a hacker, a diplomat or a straightforward gunfighter?

Designed as a throwback to earlier 2D platforming and action games combined with modern RPG elements, Dex offers real-time combat, a mature storyline and interactive dialogues.

Customize your character’s skills, equipment and even augmentations – implants which grant you superhuman abilities and open up new paths within the game’s open world.

A revolutionary hacking mechanic also lets you dive into Cyberspace: overcome viruses and intrusion countermeasures to deactivate turrets, overload devices, steal corporate data and cripple your enemies!

reviews.review:
[h1]Dex[/h1]

Some people compare this to Deus Ex. For me this is more like Splinter Cell from twenty years ago running on an old Nokia phone. I think the RPG side is more interesting than in Deus Ex, even if the gameplay can feel a bit clunky at times. Still, I was positively surprised.

[h1]Pros[/h1]

- The plot is good, and it feels like genuine effort went into the storytelling. The story is a bit clichéd, but the interactions with other characters make it feel genuine.
- One of the most intricate and believable cyberpunk worlds in a video game. You can buy condoms, sell porn mags and give antidepressants to a homeless guy.
- The map lets you fast-travel!
- You can experiment and approach situations in different ways.
- Once you get invested in the world, it's hard to stop playing.
- The 2D world feels about the right size. You can explore and do some side activities if you want, but it's not so big that you get lost, either.
- There's replay value if you want to try allocating skill points differently.
- The music is great and fits the atmosphere.

[h1]Cons[/h1]

- Combat has some weird inconsistencies. Sometimes you can stealth kill four enemies in a row without any problems, but other times the game seems to decide that's not happening and you end up spending 30 magnum rounds and two health packs clearing the same area. This can happen even when you load the same save twice.
- Health station placement can be weird. Sometimes there are none around when you need them, while other times they seem to be around every corner.
- Stealth and exploration become tedious after the first few hours. You often have no idea where to go, so you end up checking every room. Most rooms have little more than a closet and some toilet paper. You find terminals that give you yet another email or a simple note after a hacking minigame. The dock area is the worst example of exploration without much payoff: you enter a room and an enemy starts shooting at you immediately. Many rooms contain nothing but cameras and security guards. The endgame takes this to another level, with one door requiring several security cards and even seemingly empty rooms packed with guards, turrets and cameras. At some point it starts feeling ridiculous.
- Movement and melee combat can feel clunky and take some time to get used to. It can take even a full playthrough to realize how some of the mechanics work.
- Ladder climbing is buggy.
- There's too much hacking. It takes forever, and the payoff is too small for the time you have to spend on it.
- Personally, I prefer my story missions to be more linear than they are in this game. I ended up clearing several areas before I was supposed to because the instructions were iffy and the quest descriptions were roundabout. It's not too bad, but it slows the game down at certain points.
- Stealth doesn't always work as you'd expect. There's no clear indication of whether enemies have spotted you. You can hide behind containers, but sometimes a brute will just come and smack you anyway. Overall, though, stealth is tolerable and you don't have to spend too much time crouching and sneaking. I only found out late in the game that you can actually crouch and cross paths with some enemies without them noticing anything.
- Combat balancing has other issues, too. Enemies don't take fall damage, and fights can take forever if you run out of ammo and have to rely on melee attacks without any melee upgrades. One hit against a strong enemy barely takes 3% off its health, yet you can't take it down quietly. Meanwhile, it can kick and slam you from a ridiculous distance, taking more than 10% of your health with a single hit. You can pick up all kinds of ammo, but usually you can't take a gun from a dead enemy. How weird is that?

[h1]Neutral[/h1]

- Hacking feels like an intricate minigame that's better than in most games, but I don't like how quickly the MC runs out of focus.
- Some of the dialogue is really good, while other parts consist of awkward, three-word sentences. Sometimes you get a boring conversation with a character you end up having to kill anyway, making you wonder how much the dialogue actually mattered.
- The game has voice acting, but with the default audio settings, loud music can drown out some of the dialogue.

[h1]Verdict[/h1]

It's a solid cyberpunk RPG with good storytelling, although the endgame is a bit weird, missions are kinda hard to follow here and there, and the combat is not great but tolerable.

[b]Final score: 7/10[/b]
